title: How to learn better using psychology, with Regan Gurung, PhD, and John Dunlosky, PhD

sentences.en: From kindergarten to college, most students and teachers focus on mastering content, reading, writing, math, science, and history.
sentences.zh: 从幼儿园到大学，大多数学生和老师都专注于掌握内容，包括阅读、写作、数学、科学和历史。

sentences.en: But along the way, very few students are taught a crucial skill set.
sentences.zh: 但在求学过程中，很少有学生被教授一套至关重要的技能。

sentences.en: What exactly is the best way to learn?
sentences.zh: 到底什么是最好的学习方法？

sentences.en: Decades of research in psychology have found that some study techniques are far more effective than others, but the most effective teaching and
sentences.zh: 几十年的心理学研究发现，有些学习技巧远比其他方法有效，但最有效的教学和

sentences.en: learning methods are not always the most popular ones.
sentences.zh: 学习方法并不总是最受欢迎的。

sentences.en: So students end up wasting time and effort using study strategies that don't help them acquire new knowledge and get frustrated in the process.
sentences.zh: 因此，学生们最终浪费了时间和精力去使用那些无法帮助他们获取新知识的学习策略，并在过程中感到沮丧。

sentences.en: Which study techniques do work and which ones don't?
sentences.zh: 哪些学习技巧有效，哪些无效？

sentences.en: Is it useful to take copious notes, to read every section of a textbook multiple times, to highlight key points on a page?
sentences.zh: 做大量的笔记、把课本的每一节读上好几遍、在页面上高亮重点，这些真的有用吗？

sentences.en: What about cramming?
sentences.zh: 那临时抱佛脚呢？

sentences.en: Can students cram their way to an A?
sentences.zh: 学生可以通过临时抱佛脚拿到A吗？

sentences.en: And do the same study strategies work for everyone, or are there techniques that work well for some people and not for others?
sentences.zh: 同样的学习策略对每个人都有效吗？还是说有些技巧对某些人管用，对其他人却行不通？

sentences.en: What about those of us who are no longer in school?
sentences.zh: 那我们这些已经离开学校的人呢？

sentences.en: Can the same learning skills help lifelong learners master knitting or learn to retile their bathroom or acquire some other new knowledge or skill?
sentences.zh: 同样的学习技能能否帮助终身学习者掌握编织、学会重铺浴室瓷砖，或者习得其他新知识或技能？

sentences.en: Welcome to Speaking of
sentences.zh: 欢迎收听《心理学谈话》

sentences.en: Psychology, the flagship podcast of the American Psychological Association that examines the links between psychological science and everyday life.
sentences.zh: 这是美国心理学会的旗舰播客，旨在探讨心理科学与日常生活之间的联系。

sentences.en: I'm Kim Mills.
sentences.zh: 我是金·米尔斯。

sentences.en: We have two guests today.
sentences.zh: 今天我们请到了两位嘉宾。

sentences.en: They're the co-authors of a new book from APA called Study Like a Champ, the psychology-based guide to grade A study habits, which will be published in January.
sentences.zh: 他们是美国心理学会新书《像冠军一样学习：基于心理学的A级学习习惯指南》的合著者，该书将于一月出版。

sentences.en: First is Dr. Regan Gurung, a professor and director of the general psychology program at Oregon State University.
sentences.zh: 首先是里根·古隆博士，他是俄勒冈州立大学的教授，也是普通心理学项目的主任。

sentences.en: He studies social and health psychology as well as the psychology of teaching and learning.
sentences.zh: 他研究社会心理学和健康心理学，以及教学与学习心理学。

sentences.en: He's the founding editor of APA's journal Scholarship of Teaching and
sentences.zh: 他是美国心理学会（APA）旗下期刊《心理学教学与学习学术研究》的创刊编辑，

sentences.en: Learning in psychology and is a past president of the Society for Teaching of Psychology, APA's Division II.
sentences.zh: 也是美国心理学会第二分会——心理学教学协会的前任主席。

sentences.en: Before moving to Oregon in 2019, he taught at the University of Wisconsin-Green Bay for 20 years.
sentences.zh: 在2019年搬到俄勒冈州之前，他在威斯康星大学绿湾分校任教了20年。

sentences.en: Next is Dr. John Dunlosky, a professor of psychology and director of the Science of Learning and Education
sentences.zh: 接下来是约翰·邓洛斯基博士，他是肯特州立大学的心理学教授，也是学习与教育科学

sentences.en: Center at Kent State University.
sentences.zh: 中心的主任。

sentences.en: Dr. Dunlosky's research focuses on discovering techniques that students can use to improve their learning and achievement.
sentences.zh: 邓洛斯基博士的研究重点是发现学生可以用来提高学习效果和成就的技巧。

sentences.en: He is author of more than 150 peer-reviewed journal articles and has written or edited eight books, including the most recent one from APA.
sentences.zh: 他发表了150多篇同行评审期刊文章，并撰写或编辑了八本书，其中包括最近由美国心理学会出版的那一本。

sentences.en: Thank you both for joining me today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢两位今天能参加我的节目。

sentences.en: It's a pleasure to be here.
sentences.zh: 很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: Let's start with the big picture.
sentences.zh: 让我们从大局谈起。

sentences.en: Why is it important to teach students how to learn rather than just teaching them content?
sentences.zh: 为什么教学生如何学习，而不是仅仅教授知识内容，这一点如此重要？

sentences.en: How much difference does it make in terms of what they can achieve?
sentences.zh: 这在他们能取得的成就方面会有多大的影响？

sentences.en: That's a great place to start,
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的切入点，

sentences.en: Kim, because when we think about teaching and learning and college, so often we focus on content and content delivery.
sentences.zh: 金，因为当我们思考大学里的教与学时，我们往往过于关注内容本身以及内容的传授。

sentences.en: And when I say we both, I think parents, teachers, students, faculty, but the reality is to really get that content in and hang on to it for the long-term, true learning,
sentences.zh: 当我提到“我们”时，我想是指家长、老师、学生和教职员工，但现实是，要真正掌握这些内容并长期留存，实现真正的学习，

sentences.en: you've got to take a look at skills.
sentences.zh: 你必须关注学习技能。

sentences.en: You've got to take a look at techniques.
sentences.zh: 你必须得看看这些技巧。

sentences.en: And this is where the plot thickens because not every class is the same, not every discipline is the same.
sentences.zh: 而这正是问题变得复杂的地方，因为并非每门课都一样，也并非每个学科都一样。

sentences.en: And so the more you learn those basic skills, the more you learn a wide array of skills and different tools, you can then
sentences.zh: 所以，你学习的基本技能越多，掌握的技能和工具种类越广泛，你就越能够

sentences.en: use the best one for the best class to get the most long-term learning.
sentences.zh: 针对不同的课程选择最合适的方法，从而实现长期的学习效果。

sentences.en: So really our thought was, yes, content is important, but without the right skills to get that content in, you're not going to remember it for a very long time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们真正的想法是，没错，内容很重要，但如果没有掌握正确的方法来吸收这些内容，你是无法将其长期记住的。

sentences.en: And that truly was that inspiration for the two of us going, you know, we do all this research on learning.
sentences.zh: 这确实是我们两人的灵感来源，我们当时想，你知道，我们做了这么多关于学习的研究。

sentences.en: There's all this research about in the lab, but one of the reasons I loved working with John on this is both of us not only do basic research in
sentences.zh: 实验室里有各种各样的研究，但我喜欢和约翰合作的原因之一是，我们两人不仅在

sentences.en: labs, but we also work in the classroom.
sentences.zh: 实验室里做基础研究，同时也深入课堂教学。

sentences.en: And over the far too many years that we want to admit to, years of teaching, we've worked with just so many students and seen the problems that students have
sentences.zh: 在多年——多到我们都不愿承认的教学生涯中，我们接触过太多的学生，也看到了学生们

sentences.en: in the trenches as it were.
sentences.zh: 在实际学习中遇到的各种问题。

sentences.en: And that's what this endeavor is all about.
sentences.zh: 而这正是我们这项工作的意义所在。

sentences.en: We've seen what happens in the classroom.
sentences.zh: 我们亲眼目睹了课堂上发生的一切。

sentences.en: We've seen where learning fails.
sentences.zh: 我们看到了学习在哪些地方出了问题。

sentences.en: And let's put together those things that can really arm students to tackle, whichever class they're in.
sentences.zh: 让我们把这些能够真正武装学生、帮助他们应对任何课程的方法总结出来。

sentences.en: And as you nicely alluded to in the intro, not just in the classroom, anytime anybody wants to learn something, there are skills in here that can help you do it better.
sentences.zh: 正如你在开场白中提到的，这不仅适用于课堂，任何时候只要有人想学习新东西，这里面的技巧都能帮你做得更好。

sentences.en: Dr. Dunlosky, let me ask you this.
sentences.zh: 邓洛斯基博士，我想问你一个问题。

sentences.en: There are a lot of misconceptions and myths about learning and how to study.
sentences.zh: 关于学习和学习方法，存在很多误解和迷思。

sentences.en: What are some of the big ones and what are the strategies that students are using that really aren't working very well for them?
sentences.zh: 其中有哪些主要的误区？学生们正在使用哪些其实并不奏效的学习策略？

sentences.en: Dr. Dunlosky And I really love this question because I think we all hold some of these myths in different contexts is that if learning is difficult, then it must be bad.
sentences.zh: 邓洛斯基博士：我非常喜欢这个问题，因为我认为我们在不同情境下都会持有这些迷思，即如果学习感到困难，那一定是不好的。

sentences.en: It's taking you in the wrong direction.
sentences.zh: 这会让你走上错误的道路。

sentences.en: And it just turns out that many techniques that one uses to learn effectively are going to actually produce difficulties or struggles in your learning.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，许多能让你高效学习的技巧，实际上反而会在学习过程中产生困难或阻碍。

sentences.en: So, to think that, well, if I'm really struggling at something, I must not be going about it the right way is kind of a myth.
sentences.zh: 所以，认为“如果我在某件事上感到吃力，那一定是我方法不对”，这其实是一种迷思。

sentences.en: Because often, if you're not struggling, you probably aren't making progress to your learning goal.
sentences.zh: 因为通常情况下，如果你不感到吃力，你可能并没有在朝着学习目标取得进展。

sentences.en: It turns out that learning is just difficult.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，学习本身就是困难的。

sentences.en: So, to think that the only way it should happen is under easy context.
sentences.zh: 所以，认为学习只能在轻松的环境下进行，

sentences.en: And if it's difficult, I must not be good at this content.
sentences.zh: 或者认为“如果觉得难，一定是我不擅长这门课”，

sentences.en: It's a really horrible myth.
sentences.zh: 这真的是一个非常糟糕的迷思。

sentences.en: And I think it holds students back.
sentences.zh: 我认为它阻碍了学生的进步。

sentences.en: It's very relevant to your first question.
sentences.zh: 这和你刚才的第一个问题非常相关。

sentences.en: When we see the student who's frustrated because they're struggling at a particular course, it's not because they don't have the ability
sentences.zh: 当我们看到学生因为在某门课程上感到吃力而沮丧时，那并不是因为他们没有能力

sentences.en: to learn that content well and to perform well.
sentences.zh: 学好这些内容并取得好成绩。

sentences.en: They're just not approaching it with the best strategies.
sentences.zh: 只是他们没有采用最好的策略。

sentences.en: Unfortunately, the misconceptions also work in the other direction that some of the
sentences.zh: 不幸的是，这些误解也会反向作用，即一些

sentences.en: strategies that students use a lot that are easy to use actually lead to good learning, such as just rereading your textbook and so forth.
sentences.zh: 学生经常使用且容易操作的策略，比如反复阅读课本等，其实并不能带来良好的学习效果。

sentences.en: It gives you the sense of familiarity.
sentences.zh: 它会给你一种熟悉感。

sentences.en: So, you feel good about it.
sentences.zh: 所以你会感觉良好。

sentences.en: Hey, I know what this is all about.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我知道这讲的是什么了。

sentences.en: But it turns out that something that's like reading or rereading, which is a bit more passive, it doesn't lead to those gains in performance that you might expect.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，像阅读或反复阅读这种比较被动的方式，并不能带来你所期望的成绩提升。

sentences.en: It may make you feel good because, hey, this is familiar.
sentences.zh: 这可能会让你感觉良好，因为嘿，这很熟悉。

sentences.en: It's easy to do.
sentences.zh: 这很容易做到。

sentences.en: But sometimes, the pathway to success, there's going to be some struggles in there and you should expect them and embrace them.
sentences.zh: 但有时，通往成功的道路上会有一些挣扎，你应该预料到并拥抱它们。

sentences.en: So, what are some of the techniques that do work?
sentences.zh: 那么，有哪些行之有效的技巧呢？

sentences.en: What does the research say about the best way to learn something new and make it stick?
sentences.zh: 关于学习新事物并使其牢固掌握的最佳方法，研究是怎么说的？

sentences.en: Well, the good news is that there are a lot of strategies that are relatively effective.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，有很多策略是相对有效的。

sentences.en: And what Regan and I try to do was really pair down the field to just those most effective strategies that are cost-free.
sentences.zh: Regan和我真正尝试做的是将范围缩小到那些最有效且无需成本的策略。

sentences.en: Any student can use these, right?
sentences.zh: 任何学生都可以使用这些，对吧？

sentences.en: They're inexpensive, but also are going to have a relatively broad general impact on learning.
sentences.zh: 它们不仅便宜，而且对学习有相当广泛的普遍影响。

sentences.en: And many of these strategies improve students' learning in two ways.
sentences.zh: 其中许多策略以两种方式改善学生的学习。

sentences.en: They have a direct effect.
sentences.zh: 它们有直接的影响。

sentences.en: So, if you use them, it's going to boost your learning and maintenance and understanding of that content.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你使用它们，它将提升你的学习、保持和对内容的理解。

sentences.en: The second is an indirect effect where if you use these strategies, and this is where the
sentences.zh: 第二种是间接影响，如果你使用这些策略，这就是

sentences.en: struggling comes in, it's going to allow you to detect when you don't understand something, which can be extremely frustrating.
sentences.zh: 挣扎出现的地方，它会让你发现自己什么时候不理解某事，这可能会让人极其沮丧。

sentences.en: However, I'm saying that's an indirect effect of these strategies is because students should want to know what they're struggling with so that they can
sentences.zh: 然而，我说这是这些策略的间接影响，是因为学生应该想要知道他们在为什么而挣扎，以便他们可以

sentences.en: readjust, get help with some of their friends from instructors and so forth.
sentences.zh: 重新调整，从朋友、导师那里获得帮助等等。

sentences.en: So, it's kind of to meet those learning struggles.
sentences.zh: 所以，这算是为了应对那些学习上的挣扎。

sentences.en: My favorite technique actually is one of the easiest to use, and it's simply testing yourself or taking practice exams or practice retrieval.
sentences.zh: 我最喜欢的技巧实际上是最容易使用的之一，它就是简单地测试自己，或者进行模拟考试，或者练习提取记忆。

sentences.en: And the idea here is that when you try to practice retrieving something from memory, not simply just reading that content again, you get the both direct and indirect effect.
sentences.zh: 这里的想法是，当你尝试练习从记忆中提取某样东西，而不是仅仅再次阅读该内容时，你会同时获得直接和间接的影响。

sentences.en: If you can retrieve content accurately from memory, it turns out you get this wonderful boost in your long-term retention of that content.
sentences.zh: 如果你能准确地从记忆中提取内容，事实证明，你对该内容的长期记忆会得到极大的提升。

sentences.en: However, if you can't retrieve it yet or you struggle retrieving it, it's a really good signal that you need to do more to learn that content.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你还不能提取它，或者在提取时感到挣扎，这是一个非常好的信号，表明你需要做更多的工作来学习该内容。

sentences.en: So, here's a strategy that produces these inherent struggles that might be frustrating, but those frustrations then can lead to subsequent successes
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个产生内在挣扎的策略，可能会令人沮丧，但这些挫折随后可以带来后续的成功，

sentences.en: as students learn to hone in on what they're struggling with so they can bridge those difficulties.
sentences.zh: 因为学生学会了专注于他们正在挣扎的地方，以便他们可以克服这些困难。

sentences.en: So, that's one of many strategies that we discuss in the book.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是我们在书中讨论的众多策略之一。

sentences.en: Dr. Goering, any others that you want to put out there?
sentences.zh: Goering博士，还有什么你想提出来的吗？

sentences.en: Dr. Yeah, you know, I'm glad John jumped in on that one because I was thinking, wow, there are so many we want to talk about.
sentences.zh: 博士，是的，你知道，我很高兴John插话说了这一点，因为我在想，哇，我们想谈的太多了。

sentences.en: There is another strategy, but I'm going to tease you or not even go to that strategy and say, even before we think about strategies, we've actually
sentences.zh: 还有另一个策略，但我打算卖个关子，甚至不去谈那个策略，而是说，甚至在我们考虑策略之前，我们实际上

sentences.en: got to prepare for how we are going to learn.
sentences.zh: 必须为我们将如何学习做好准备。

sentences.en: And I think something that we spend a lot of time on right up front, you know, we start with some myths, but really the place we start is planning,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们花了很多时间在最前面做的事情，你知道，我们从一些误区开始，但我们真正开始的地方是规划，

sentences.en: because a large part of learning and I mean, you know, whether it's life in general or college,
sentences.zh: 因为学习的很大一部分，我的意思是，你知道，无论是生活还是大学，

sentences.en: where the average student is taking five classes, you know, that's a lot, that's a lot of content, that's a lot to learn.
sentences.zh: 平均学生要上五门课，你知道，那很多，那有很多内容，有很多要学。

sentences.en: That's why one of the first things we say is you've got to make sure you have a good plan down, you know, work out a good way to schedule when you're going to study,
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们说的第一件事就是你必须确保有一个好的计划，你知道，制定一个好的时间表，安排你什么时候学习，

sentences.en: when you're going to learn.
sentences.zh: 什么时候学习。

sentences.en: So, even before we get to repeat, you know, retrieval practice or testing yourself, make sure you have a good plan for when you're going to study.
sentences.zh: 所以，甚至在我们进行重复，你知道，提取练习或测试自己之前，确保你有一个好的学习时间计划。

sentences.en: When are you going to study?
sentences.zh: 你什么时候学习？

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: If you've got five classes, when in the week you study becomes really important.
sentences.zh: 如果你有五门课，你在一周内什么时候学习就变得非常重要了。

sentences.en: So, I think planning is a very, very big part of learning that somehow falls off the radar when we think about strategy.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为规划是学习中非常、非常重要的一部分，当我们考虑策略时，它不知何故被忽视了。

sentences.en: So, I want to make sure that it's up front and good.
sentences.zh: 所以，我想确保它被放在首位且做得很好。

sentences.en: Planning is really important.
sentences.zh: 规划真的很重要。

sentences.en: Right next to planning, and even before we get to retrieval practice, I want to pick up
sentences.zh: 紧挨着规划，甚至在我们进行提取练习之前，我想接着

sentences.en: something that, on something that you said in your intro, which was the copious notes, right?
sentences.zh: 你在介绍中说的一点，那就是大量的笔记，对吧？

sentences.en: Right there is when John and I look out at our classrooms, we shared this very early in the writing process, something we noticed is that students aren't taking notes as much.
sentences.zh: 就在那里，当John和我环顾我们的教室时，我们在写作过程的早期就分享了这一点，我们注意到学生记笔记没那么多了。

sentences.en: And boy, whether it's you listening to a master class on cooking or, you know, taking an online class or sitting in one of our
sentences.zh: 天哪，无论是你听烹饪大师课，还是，你知道，上在线课程，或者坐在我们的

sentences.en: classes, note-taking is one of those hidden gems where note-taking is a strategy in itself.
sentences.zh: 课堂里，记笔记是那些隐藏的宝石之一，记笔记本身就是一种策略。

sentences.en: And I think we have to realize that the process of taking notes actually helps us organize out the material and is a tool in itself that is vastly underutilized.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们必须意识到，记笔记的过程实际上帮助我们整理材料，它本身就是一个被严重低估的工具。

sentences.en: So, my first big, you know, I said, we've got a plan, we've got to make sure we take good notes, and then I'm going to hand the pass over to John to go for
sentences.zh: 所以，我的第一个大点，你知道，我说过，我们必须有一个计划，我们必须确保我们记好笔记，然后我要把接力棒传给John，去讲

sentences.en: the next big one, which is spacing and spacing out your studying.
sentences.zh: 下一个大点，那就是间隔学习，把你的学习分散开来。

sentences.en: John, there's the pass.
sentences.zh: John，接力棒给你。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Yeah, it turns out that spacing your practice is very important strategy to use.
sentences.zh: 是的，事实证明，分散你的练习是一个非常重要的策略。

sentences.en: And note, this is actually important misconception about spacing that many students hold, many
sentences.zh: 请注意，关于间隔学习，许多学生和许多

sentences.en: instructors hold, is that spacing merely means that I'm going to study for a course on more than one occasion, okay?
sentences.zh: 导师持有一个重要的误解，即间隔仅仅意味着我将在不止一个场合学习一门课程，好吗？

sentences.en: That's a very good thing to do.
sentences.zh: 那是一件非常好的事情。

sentences.en: It means you're just not cramming.
sentences.zh: 这意味着你只是没有临时抱佛脚。

sentences.en: But spacing means studying the same content in one or more sessions.
sentences.zh: 但间隔意味着在一次或多次会议中学习相同的内容。

sentences.en: So, just not studying in one or more sessions.
sentences.zh: 所以，不仅仅是在一次或多次会议中学习。

sentences.en: And note, once I say this, while you have to study in one or more sessions, it kind of ties that bow with what Regan was saying about planning.
sentences.zh: 请注意，一旦我说了这一点，虽然你必须在一次或多次会议中学习，但这与Regan关于规划的说法不谋而合。

sentences.en: In order to use some of these strategies with fidelity, students need to manage their time.
sentences.zh: 为了忠实地使用其中一些策略，学生需要管理他们的时间。

sentences.en: That is, set up multiple, say, study sessions for each class prior to an exam to get ready for it.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，在考试前为每门课安排多次学习会议，为考试做好准备。

sentences.en: Because if you just wait to cram the night before, which I'm not suggesting students don't do, that is, all students cram, just that you do more than that.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你只是等到前一天晚上才临时抱佛脚，我并不是说学生不这样做，也就是说，所有学生都会临时抱佛脚，只是说你要做的不仅仅是这些。

sentences.en: And you're going to have to plan and manage your time accordingly to take advantage of this really impactful strategy,
sentences.zh: 你将不得不相应地计划和管理你的时间，以利用这个非常有影响力的策略，

sentences.en: which by the way, students use in every other context they learn in, except for in educational context.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，学生在他们学习的每一个其他环境中都会使用它，除了在教育环境中。

sentences.en: It's a really effective strategy.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常有效的策略。

sentences.en: We just forget about it when we start studying for our classes.
sentences.zh: 当我们开始为课程学习时，我们只是忘记了它。

sentences.en: So, when you talk about spacing, is there some ideal, I mean, how much do you space things out?
sentences.zh: 所以，当你谈到间隔时，有没有什么理想的状态，我的意思是，你把事情分散到什么程度？

sentences.en: And I think you've also found interleaving is effective as well.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为你也发现交替练习也是有效的。

sentences.en: Maybe you can explain what that means.
sentences.zh: 也许你可以解释一下那意味着什么。

sentences.en: First, there's no definitive answer to how much you should space your practice.
sentences.zh: 首先，关于你应该如何分散你的练习，没有明确的答案。

sentences.en: In fact, how much is going to depend on, in kind of technical terms, the forgetting rate for the particular content.
sentences.zh: 事实上，多少取决于，用技术术语来说，特定内容的遗忘率。

sentences.en: Because the idea is that you want to come back to that material right before you're going to forget it.
sentences.zh: 因为想法是，你想在即将忘记材料之前回到它。

sentences.en: And for different kinds of material, depending on your background, that interval might be different lengths.
sentences.zh: 对于不同类型的材料，根据你的背景，那个间隔的长度可能会有所不同。

sentences.en: The good news is, I don't think we have to have a definitive answer for students.
sentences.zh: 好消息是，我不认为我们必须给学生一个明确的答案。

sentences.en: Because often, how much you want to space your practice is defined by your syllabus.
sentences.zh: 因为通常，你想如何分散你的练习是由你的教学大纲定义的。

sentences.en: You'll have so many exams over this space of a semester, and you have, say, three or four weeks to study for each exam.
sentences.zh: 你在一个学期内会有很多次考试，并且你有，比如说，三到四周的时间为每次考试学习。

sentences.en: So, that's about how much time you have to prepare.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是你准备考试所剩的时间。

sentences.en: So, typically, I recommend if students can study twice a week for a particular class, well, the spacing will be two or three days to space that practice out, which is pretty good.
sentences.zh: 通常，如果学生能每周为某门课学习两次，我会建议将练习间隔开两到三天，这样效果相当不错。

sentences.en: I think if students would put on their schedules,
sentences.zh: 我认为如果学生能把这些安排进日程表，

sentences.en: I'm going to study for each class twice a week and come back to the same material in every one of
sentences.zh: 比如“我每周要为每门课学习两次，并且在每次学习中都回顾相同的内容”，

sentences.en: those sessions, they'll see a really nice benefit to their performance because they're spacing their practice.
sentences.zh: 他们会发现这对学习表现有非常好的促进作用，因为他们采用了间隔练习法。

sentences.en: Now, with respect to interleaving, that's kind of a complicated strategy.
sentences.zh: 至于交替练习，这是一种比较复杂的策略。

sentences.en: And it means that you're going to study different content intermixed.
sentences.zh: 它的意思是你要将不同的学习内容混合在一起进行复习。

sentences.en: And specifically, it works well for content that you get confused about or that you would confuse with one another.
sentences.zh: 具体来说，它非常适合处理那些容易混淆的内容。

sentences.en: So, imagine studying for a math exam.
sentences.zh: 想象一下你在准备数学考试。

sentences.en: And you know you're going to be tested on a variety of different math problems, say, different calculus problems where you have to differentiate equations and so forth.
sentences.zh: 你知道考试会涉及各种不同的数学问题，比如微积分中需要求导的方程等等。

sentences.en: One of the difficulties of doing that, and there are many of solving those kinds of problems, is just identifying exactly what kind of problem this is.
sentences.zh: 解决这类问题的一大难点，其实也是解决很多问题时的难点，就在于准确识别出这到底是什么类型的问题。

sentences.en: Interleaving gives students the practice of comparing and contrasting different probleMs. So, the first thing they need to do
sentences.zh: 交替练习能让学生通过比较和对比不同的问题来获得锻炼。所以，他们首先要做的是

sentences.en: is to identify what kind of problem is this and hence, what solution should I have?
sentences.zh: 识别出这是什么类型的问题，从而确定我应该使用什么解法？

sentences.en: Typically, however, most students and most textbooks are set up this way so that you practice the same kind of problem in mass.
sentences.zh: 然而，大多数学生和教材通常都是这样安排的：让你集中练习同一种类型的问题。

sentences.en: So, when you go to the next one, you know exactly what kind of problem it is.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你做下一道题时，你已经完全知道它是哪种类型了。

sentences.en: You're practicing just can I apply the right solution.
sentences.zh: 你练习的仅仅是“我能否应用正确的解法”。

sentences.en: So, interleaving actually helps students to mix up different problems so they can get better at identifying what kind of problem is this and then how should I solve it.
sentences.zh: 因此，交替练习实际上能帮助学生混合不同的问题，从而提高他们识别问题类型并确定解法的能力。

sentences.en: Quite frankly, one of the biggest benefits of interleaving is that it forces students to space practice.
sentences.zh: 坦白说，交替练习最大的好处之一是它迫使学生进行间隔练习。

sentences.en: Because by the necessity, if you're interleaving different concepts and coming back to the old ones, you'll also have a lot of space practice in your interleaved practice.
sentences.zh: 因为如果你必须交替学习不同的概念并不断回顾旧知识，你的交替练习中自然也会包含大量的间隔练习。

sentences.en: We talk a lot about the details about how to implement this in the book because they're a little bit more complicated than we can portray in the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们在书中详细讨论了如何实施这一点，因为它们比我们在播客中能呈现的要复杂一些。

sentences.en: But all of these can be, again, easily used by students as long as they manage their time and plan for different study episodes for each class.
sentences.zh: 但只要学生能管理好时间并为每门课规划不同的学习环节，这些方法都可以轻松应用。

sentences.en: Dr. Gurung, you were talking a little while ago about preparing, how it's important for a student to prepare to study.
sentences.zh: Gurung 博士，您刚才提到准备工作，提到学生为学习做好准备非常重要。

sentences.en: And I'm wondering, does it matter your surroundings, where you study?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，学习环境，也就是你在哪里学习，这有关系吗？

sentences.en: And some people like to have music in the background.
sentences.zh: 有些人喜欢在背景中放点音乐。

sentences.en: Is that something that makes your studying more or less effective?
sentences.zh: 这会让你的学习效率变高还是变低呢？

sentences.en: Does it vary from person to person?
sentences.zh: 这会因人而异吗？

sentences.en: Dr. So, yeah, distractions are something pretty big to focus on.
sentences.zh: 博士：是的，干扰因素确实是专注力的一大敌人。

sentences.en: And when we think about distractions, you know, I wish it was only music.
sentences.zh: 当我们谈到干扰时，你知道，我希望仅仅是音乐的问题。

sentences.en: But for the average person, let alone the average student, but the average person, there's a cell phone around.
sentences.zh: 但对于普通人，更不用说普通学生了，身边总是有手机。

sentences.en: There may be, you know, Instagram or Facebook, if you're an oldie, you know, or Twitter, or maybe Mastodon now.
sentences.zh: 可能还有 Instagram 或 Facebook（如果你年纪大一点的话），或者 Twitter，现在可能还有 Mastodon。

sentences.en: You know, it's all these things all around.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这些东西无处不在。

sentences.en: But very often people, I think, believe that, you know, music is good and soothing.
sentences.zh: 但很多人往往认为，音乐是好的，是舒缓的。

sentences.en: And what's really interesting about especially music is that just the key thing for us to remember is just
sentences.zh: 关于音乐，真正有趣且我们需要记住的关键点是，

sentences.en: anything that's using mental energy is taking energy away from what we're focusing on.
sentences.zh: 任何消耗心理能量的事物都会从我们专注的事情中夺走能量。

sentences.en: That's something really at the basic core.
sentences.zh: 这是最核心的基本原则。

sentences.en: If I am trying to read something, if there's a conversation around me, if there's music around me, if the TV is on and something is streaming, a part of my brain that would
sentences.zh: 如果我试图阅读，周围有人在交谈，有音乐，电视开着且在播放流媒体内容，那么我大脑中本该

sentences.en: be paying attention to what I'm reading is now paying attention to some of those other facts.
sentences.zh: 用于关注阅读内容的区域，现在却在关注那些干扰信息。

sentences.en: When you think about it from, especially when we think about it from a neuroscience perspective
sentences.zh: 当你从神经科学的角度，特别是从认知神经科学的角度来思考时，

sentences.en: and a cognitive neuroscience perspective, one way to think about it is, or to remember is, our working memory has a limited capacity.
sentences.zh: 一种理解或记住它的方式是：我们的工作记忆容量是有限的。

sentences.en: It's got a limited capacity and it's got a limited duration where we can store material.
sentences.zh: 它的容量有限，存储材料的持续时间也有限。

sentences.en: So our task is to take material from working memory and get it into long-term memory.
sentences.zh: 所以我们的任务是将材料从工作记忆转移到长期记忆中。

sentences.en: And one of the best things we can do to help our brains move things from working memory to long-term memory is to pay attention and focus on what we're reading and doing.
sentences.zh: 而帮助大脑将信息从工作记忆转移到长期记忆的最佳方法之一，就是专注于你正在阅读和做的事情。

sentences.en: Because the more we focus on it, the better we can get things to long-term memory.
sentences.zh: 因为我们越专注，就越能更好地将信息存入长期记忆。

sentences.en: Now mind you, retrieval practice is another one of those things that strengthens the memories in long-term memories and this all ties together.
sentences.zh: 当然，提取练习也是增强长期记忆中记忆的手段之一，这些都是相互关联的。

sentences.en: But going all the way back to your question, the setting in which you study can make the world of a difference.
sentences.zh: 回到你的问题，你学习的环境确实会产生巨大的影响。

sentences.en: And a nice bottom line is if you can cut down on distractions, the more you can focus on what you're studying, the more likely you are to pay attention to it, the deeper you are
sentences.zh: 结论很简单：如果你能减少干扰，你就能越专注于学习内容，就越有可能关注它，处理得越深，

sentences.en: likely to process it, which in turn is related to longer-term memory.
sentences.zh: 这反过来又与长期记忆有关。

sentences.en: Let's talk for a minute about something called learning styles.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈所谓的“学习风格”。

sentences.en: APA published a study last year challenging the belief among many, including educators, that learning styles are set at birth and that they predict academic and career success.
sentences.zh: 美国心理学会（APA）去年发表了一项研究，挑战了包括教育工作者在内的许多人的信念，即学习风格是天生的，且能预测学业和职业成就。

sentences.en: Do either of you believe that people have an inherent learning style, whether that's auditory, visual or tactical, and that it's necessary to teach to those styles?
sentences.zh: 你们中有人认为人们有固有的学习风格吗？无论是听觉型、视觉型还是触觉型，并且有必要针对这些风格进行教学吗？

sentences.en: Based on all the evidence,
sentences.zh: 基于所有的证据，

sentences.en: Kim, my conclusion is that no, people do not have learning styles.
sentences.zh: Kim，我的结论是：不，人们并没有所谓的学习风格。

sentences.en: They do have learning preferences and those I validate and respect.
sentences.zh: 他们确实有学习偏好，我对此表示认可和尊重。

sentences.en: Some people like to see things visually.
sentences.zh: 有些人喜欢视觉化地看东西。

sentences.en: Some people like to hear them, feel them, touch them, but those preferences don't translate into learning outcomes.
sentences.zh: 有些人喜欢听、感受或触摸，但这些偏好并不能转化为学习成果。

sentences.en: And one simple example would be is, let's say you're a auditory learner and I'm teaching you and we'll go back to calculus.
sentences.zh: 举个简单的例子，假设你是听觉型学习者，我正在教你，我们回到微积分的话题。

sentences.en: And I can either describe the equations in words to you because you're auditory or I can show you by drawing the equations up on the board.
sentences.zh: 我可以口头描述方程，因为你是听觉型的，或者我可以在黑板上画出方程展示给你看。

sentences.en: It doesn't take lots of thinking to realize that the most effective technique there for you, regardless of your preference, is to write this on the board because
sentences.zh: 不需要多想就能意识到，对你来说最有效的技术，无论你的偏好如何，都是把方程写在黑板上，因为

sentences.en: it would be very difficult to decipher all of that verbally.
sentences.zh: 仅靠口头描述来解读所有这些内容是非常困难的。

sentences.en: It just turns out that some content is best taught and best learned using a particular modality, whether it's visual, auditory, maybe multiple modalities.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，某些内容最适合通过特定的方式来教授和学习，无论是视觉、听觉，还是多种方式结合。

sentences.en: But to think that its structure is going to benefit their students by figuring out what
sentences.zh: 但认为教师通过找出每个人的风格并针对该风格进行教学就能让学生受益，这不仅在课堂上

sentences.en: every style someone has and then teaching to that style is not only something that's probably not
sentences.zh: 可能无法有效实现，而且实际上也不应该这样做，因为它不会带来更好的学习收益。

sentences.en: going to happen in the classroom effectively, but really shouldn't happen because it's not going to lead to better gains in learning.
sentences.zh: 这是我的观点，也许 Regan 对此有不同的看法。

sentences.en: So that's my own perspective, but maybe Regan has got a different spin on all of this.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我实际上想补充一点，并聚焦于教师的角色，

sentences.en: Well, you know, I'm actually going to add to that and hone in on the instructor part,
sentences.zh: 因为我认为这里真正重要的是，首先，积累的证据表明学习风格更多处于“神话”层面。

sentences.en: because I think what's really important here is, first off, the accumulated evidence that suggests that learning styles are more the myth level.
sentences.zh: 2007 年 Batchelor 及其同事发表了一篇很棒的文章，我认为它几乎给“学习风格在课堂中很重要”这一观念敲响了丧钟。

sentences.en: There was a great article that actually came out in 2007 by Batchelor and colleagues that pretty much put the final nail, I think, in this notion that,
sentences.zh: 但我认为经常被忽略的一点，John 也提到了，但我真的想强调一下，那就是教师将教学风格与学习风格相匹配，

sentences.en: you know, learning styles are important in the classroom.
sentences.zh: 已被证明并不是一种有效的教学方式。

sentences.en: But I think what's often missed, and John alluded to this, but I really want to underscore it, is that the teacher matching a
sentences.zh: 事实上，几年前我自己也做过一项研究，我们发表了一项研究，

sentences.en: teaching style to a learning style has just not been found to be an effective way to go.
sentences.zh: 专门为了验证这一点，修改了教学风格以匹配学习风格。

sentences.en: And in fact, I mean, actually, I did a study on this myself where we, some years ago, where we published a study
sentences.zh: 结果完全没有任何效果。

sentences.en: actually modifying learning style, a teaching style for a learning style, just to put it to the teSt.
sentences.zh: 积累的证据甚至更进一步表明，你准备好听了吗？

sentences.en: Absolutely no effects whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 学生实际上从教师使用多种风格中受益更多。

sentences.en: And the accumulated evidence goes even further to say that, are you ready for it?
sentences.zh: 所以这不仅仅是“请用我的风格教我”，而是“不，如果我的老师使用多种风格，我实际上学得更好”。

sentences.en: Students actually benefit from instructors using different styles.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要，因为我知道 John 和我都听过学生说：“哦，我不喜欢那门课，我是视觉型学习者，但他们用了其他风格。”

sentences.en: So it's not just, please teach me in my style, it's no, I'm actually going to learn better if my instructor is using multiple styles.
sentences.zh: “我希望他们用我的风格。”

sentences.en: And this is so important because I know John and I have both heard students say, oh, I don't like that class there.
sentences.zh: 在这里，数据表明，不，实际上作为教师使用不同的风格，对你作为学生和学习者来说，比我们试图匹配风格要好得多。

sentences.en: I'm such a visual learner, but they use some other style.
sentences.zh: 所以不要责怪老师。

sentences.en: I wish they used my style.
sentences.zh: 是的，不要责怪老师。

sentences.en: Here, the data says, no, actually, that using different styles as an instructor is way better for you as a student and a learner than if we actually tried to match styles.
sentences.zh: 数据表明多种教学风格更好。

sentences.en: So don't blame the instructor.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要，因为尽管数据在 07 年就出来了，但我仍看到最近的调查，

sentences.en: Yeah, don't blame the instructor.
sentences.zh: 特别是在 K-12（幼儿园到高中）教学中，这种学习风格的观念依然存在。

sentences.en: The data says multiple teaching styles are better.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这已经是老掉牙的事情了。

sentences.en: And this is so important because, you know, even though the data came out in 07, I've seen even recent surveys
sentences.zh: 我们继续吧。

sentences.en: of particularly K through 12 instruction, where this notion of learning style still persists.
sentences.zh: 让我们专注于真正有帮助的事情，比如提取练习和间隔练习。

sentences.en: You know, it's been there, done that long time ago.
sentences.zh: 我们的挑战在于，如何帮助学生练习这些能帮助他们学习的技能和技巧。

sentences.en: Let's move on.
sentences.zh: 这是更大的挑战。

sentences.en: Let's focus on things that actually help, like, you know, retrieval practice and spacing practice.
sentences.zh: 学习需要记忆的内容（比如拼写或乘法表）和学习需要对概念或思想有更深理解的内容，这两者之间有区别吗？

sentences.en: That's our challenge, is how do we help our students practice these skills, these techniques that will help them learn.
sentences.zh: 你们谈到的技巧对这两种学习都有帮助吗？

sentences.en: That's the bigger challenge.
sentences.zh: 我会说答案是肯定的。

sentences.en: Is there a difference between learning something that requires memorization, say,
sentences.zh: 许多通用策略确实被建立起来，且许多人认为它们能促进内容的记忆和保持。

sentences.en: spelling or the multiplication tables, and learning something that requires a deeper understanding of concepts or ideas?
sentences.zh: 比如提取练习，你从记忆中提取某样东西，以后就能记得更牢。

sentences.en: Can the techniques that you're talking about help with both of those types of learning?
sentences.zh: 所以，这里的观点是，很多时候理解力被——我不想说被高估或过度吹捧了。

sentences.en: I would say the answer is yes.
sentences.zh: 它非常重要。

sentences.en: Many of the general strategies certainly are set up and many believe promote memory and retention of the content.
sentences.zh: 但我认为发生的情况是，记忆力被低估了。

sentences.en: Something like retrieval practice, well, you retrieve something from memory and you remember it better later on.
sentences.zh: 例如，如果我记不住，我怎么能应用一个已经理解的概念并使用它呢？

sentences.en: So, the idea here, though, is that much of comprehension is, I don't want to say overrated or over touted.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里的观点是，我们越是利用这些记忆策略来学习需要理解的困难内容，

sentences.en: It's very important.
sentences.zh: 我们在需要时就越能调用这些内容。

sentences.en: But I think what happens is that memory is underrated.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们描述的这些策略是所有学习的灵丹妙药吗？

sentences.en: So, for instance, how can I, say, apply a concept that is comprehended and use it if I don't remember it?
sentences.zh: 它们在所有情况下都能帮到你吗？

sentences.en: So, the idea here is the more we use these memorization strategies to learn difficult content
sentences.zh: 绝对不是。

sentences.en: that requires comprehension, the more we'll have that content available to us when we subscribe.
sentences.zh: 但它们不仅有助于巩固记忆部分，也有助于帮助学生理解。

sentences.en: So, are any of these strategies that we describe, are they the panacea of all learning?
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，仅仅使用提取练习就能同时促进记忆和保持。

sentences.en: So, are they going to help you in all cases?
sentences.zh: 话虽如此，它并不总能促进最高水平的理解。

sentences.en: Absolutely not.
sentences.zh: 因此，学生需要做更多的事情，比如向自己解释内容。

sentences.en: But they help chip away not only at the retention component, but also helping students understand.
sentences.zh: 例如，去听讲座，这样他们可以听到老师解释内容。

sentences.en: So, yes, just using retrieval practice can promote both memory and retention.
sentences.zh: 他们可以将这种教学与尝试向自己解释或与老师交流结合起来，

sentences.en: That said, it won't always promote the highest levels of comprehension.
sentences.zh: 利用这些其他技巧来真正巩固他们的理解。

sentences.en: So, students would need to do more, such as explain content to themselves.
sentences.zh: 因为我们不仅会忘记乘法表，也可能会忘记对微积分的理解。

sentences.en: Say, for instance, go to a lecture so they can hear the instructor explain the content.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我们必须回去重复练习或解决那些问题，以实现对理解和概念的长期保持。

sentences.en: And they can supplement this kind of instruction in trying to explain things to themselves or talk to their instructor with these
sentences.zh: 这就是我对它的看法。

sentences.en: other techniques to really solidify their understanding.
sentences.zh: 这些方法在各方面都有帮助。

sentences.en: Because not only can we, say, forget our multiplication tables, but we can always also forget our understanding of, say, calculus.
sentences.zh: 但学生需要多种策略才能真正掌握任何特定的内容。

sentences.en: And that's why we have to go back and repeat, say, practicing or solving of those problems to lead to long-term retention of understanding and comprehension.
sentences.zh: Kim，也许我可以举一个非常实用的例子来补充。

sentences.en: So, that's kind of my spin on it.
sentences.zh: 以抽认卡这个经典例子为例。

sentences.en: These can help in all ways.
sentences.zh: 很多学生，特别是在大型入门课中，都在使用抽认卡。

sentences.en: But students are going to need multiple strategies to really master any particular content.
sentences.zh: 经典的教学法当然是一面写术语，另一面写定义。

sentences.en: And Kim, maybe I can add by a really pragmatic example.
sentences.zh: 当然，越来越多的学生使用电子版，但理念是一样的。

sentences.en: And so, take a classic example of flashcards.
sentences.zh: 有一个术语，你点击一下，它就会闪现出定义。

sentences.en: A lot of students, especially in large introductory classes, use flashcards.
sentences.zh: 这听起来像是死记硬背，对吧？

sentences.en: And the classic methodology, of course, is you have your term on one side and the definition on the other.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，对吧？

sentences.en: Of course, more and more students are using it electronically, but the idea is the same.
sentences.zh: 但正如 John 所说，这也非常重要。

sentences.en: There's a term and you click something and it flashes to the definition.
sentences.zh: 但这就是我们谈论更进一步的地方。

sentences.en: Now, that sounds like memorization, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，在经典抽认卡的基础上，有两个简单的步骤。

sentences.en: And it is, right?
sentences.zh: 如果第一步是一面写术语，另一面写教材定义，那么一个非常好的第二步是让学生用自己的话写出定义，对吧？

sentences.en: But it's also, as John said, really important.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们有了教材定义。

sentences.en: But here's where we talk about going further.
sentences.zh: 现在，他们正在处理这些材料，用自己的话写出来。

sentences.en: So, a really nice way to go, two simple steps beyond the classic flashcard.
sentences.zh: 还有第三步，这才是真正通向学习的路径。

sentences.en: So, if step one is term on one side, textbook definition on the other, a really good second step is the student now writing the definition in their own words, right?
sentences.zh: 所以，你有教材定义。

sentences.en: So, they've got the textbook definition.
sentences.zh: 你有用自己的话写的定义。

sentences.en: Now, they're doing something with that material, writing it in their own words.
sentences.zh: 现在，想出一个例子，对吧？

sentences.en: There's a third step that really goes towards learning.
sentences.zh: 通过这种应用，对吧？

sentences.en: So, you've got the textbook definition.
sentences.zh: 这就是 John 谈到的提升到更高学习水平的时候。

sentences.en: You've got the definition in your own words.
sentences.zh: 通过拿那张简单的基础抽认卡，用自己的话复述，然后想出一个应用场景，你几乎可以保证能更好地记住那个概念。

sentences.en: Now, come up with an example, right?
sentences.zh: 我说“几乎保证”是因为我有数据表明，这种我们称之为“抽认卡加强法”的方法，

sentences.en: And by that application, right?
sentences.zh: 在测验中确实比仅使用标准抽认卡方法能带来更好的学习效果。

sentences.en: And that's when John was talking about going to a higher level of learning.
sentences.zh: 特别感谢 Drew Appleby，他最早向我介绍了这种想法。

sentences.en: By taking that simple basic flashcard and going, putting it into your own words and then coming up with an application, you are near guaranteed to remember that concept better.
sentences.zh: 我们已经测试过了，果然有效，超越基础知识是非常重要的。

sentences.en: And I say near guaranteed because I've got data showing that this method, what we call the flashcard plus method, actually
sentences.zh: 我认为太频繁了，我希望 John 有机会谈谈我所说的经典之作，

sentences.en: results in higher learning on quizzes than if you just use the standard flashcard method.
sentences.zh: 即 Dunlosky 等人 2013 年的论文。

sentences.en: And a big shout out to Drew Appleby, who first introduced me to this kind of idea.
sentences.zh: 我之所以这样提，是因为 John 确实说过：看，这些是学生经常做的 10 件事，但它们的效用各不相同。

sentences.en: But we've tested it, and sure enough, it's doing something, going beyond that basics, that's important.
sentences.zh: 我认为这里重要的是，我们大多数人对需要做什么都有个概念。

sentences.en: And I think far too often, I'm hoping John has a chance to talk a little bit about what I refer to as the classic
sentences.zh: 但其中许多事情并不一定是最好的学习方式。

sentences.en: Donlowski et al 2013 paper.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么有研究结果出来非常好，它告诉你：你知道吗，你可能觉得高亮标记很棒。

sentences.en: But the reason I refer to it that way is John really said, look, here are these 10 things that students often do, but here's how they vary in their utility.
sentences.zh: 是的，你给我看了你那本用五种颜色高亮标记的教科书。

sentences.en: And I think, what I think is important here is most of us have an idea of what we need to do.
sentences.zh: 那可能不行，而且，你知道，我们经常看到这种情况。

sentences.en: Many of those things aren't necessarily the best way for learning.
sentences.zh: 我们来谈谈学习风格吧。

sentences.en: And I think that's why it's so nice to have research out there that says, you know what, you may have thought highlighting is great.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是你准备考试所剩的时间。

sentences.en: Yes, you've shown me your textbook with all the five colors highlighting.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是你准备考试所剩的时间。

sentences.en: That may not, and then that, you know, that we see that often.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是你准备考试所剩的时间。

sentences.en: That's not necessarily the best way to learn.
sentences.zh: 那未必是最好的学习方式。

sentences.en: You've also talked about the importance of taking good notes.
sentences.zh: 你也提到过做笔记的重要性。

sentences.en: And I believe you have found that there's a difference between whether you take notes by hand or on your laptop.
sentences.zh: 而且我相信你发现，手写笔记和用笔记本电脑做笔记是有区别的。

sentences.en: What's happening in our brains if one is better than the other, and which is better?
sentences.zh: 如果其中一种方式更好，我们的大脑会发生什么？哪种方式更好呢？

sentences.en: Actually, I've done quite a bit of research on this recently, Kim.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我最近在这方面做了不少研究，金。

sentences.en: So let me kind of jump in here.
sentences.zh: 所以让我来插一句。

sentences.en: And the bottom line is that the, taken as a whole, the evidence indicates that neither pathway to taking notes is better than the other, whether you're longhand or typing.
sentences.zh: 底线是，总的来说，证据表明无论是手写还是打字，这两种做笔记的方式并没有哪种更好。

sentences.en: And I won't get into the nitty gritty of all of this because I want to point out something that I think is more important than whether you're using longhand or a computer, okay?
sentences.zh: 我不会深入探讨所有细节，因为我想指出一点，我认为这比你用手写还是用电脑更重要，好吗？

sentences.en: Which I'd recommend whatever students like the best and what they think is most effective for a particular class they go with, okay?
sentences.zh: 我建议学生们选择自己最喜欢、认为对特定课程最有效的方式，好吗？

sentences.en: The little hidden secret of all the research on note-taking is called the control group.
sentences.zh: 关于做笔记的所有研究中，有一个小小的隐藏秘密，那就是对照组。

sentences.en: And the control group in these experiments, they sit and they just listen to a lecture.
sentences.zh: 在这些实验中，对照组的学生只是坐在那里听讲座。

sentences.en: They don't take any notes, okay?
sentences.zh: 他们不做任何笔记，好吗？

sentences.en: So now I'm going to compare students' knowledge about that lecture, whether they've taken no notes, the control group, or whether they've taken notes longhand or with a computer.
sentences.zh: 现在我要比较学生们对讲座内容的掌握程度，无论他们是不做笔记的对照组，还是手写或用电脑做笔记的学生。

sentences.en: And in many, many cases, none of those groups differ in how much they retain.
sentences.zh: 在很多很多情况下，这些组在知识留存方面并没有区别。

sentences.en: That is, just sitting listening to a lecture, you're going to retain about as much as you do by taking notes.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，仅仅坐在那里听讲座，你留存的知识量和做笔记差不多。

sentences.en: However, none of the groups retain that much at all.
sentences.zh: 然而，没有任何一组能留存多少知识。

sentences.en: None of the groups retain that much.
sentences.zh: 没有任何一组能留存多少知识。

sentences.en: So this is the key.
sentences.zh: 所以这是关键所在。

sentences.en: The group who doesn't take notes, well, they're pretty much behind the eight ball now because they don't have anything to study to prepare themselves for the exam.
sentences.zh: 不做笔记的那组人，他们现在处于非常不利的境地，因为他们没有任何资料可以复习来准备考试。

sentences.en: So when we talk about the importance of notes, you don't necessarily get a lot out of taking them.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们谈论笔记的重要性时，做笔记本身并不一定能让你收获很多。

sentences.en: But what you need to do is have good complete notes because the real learning is going to happen after the fact and how you interact and study those notes moving forward.
sentences.zh: 但你需要做的是拥有完整的好笔记，因为真正的学习发生在此之后，以及你之后如何与这些笔记互动和复习。

sentences.en: So my recommendation, if you're in a class, say, where a teacher talks really, really fast, well, you might be better
sentences.zh: 所以我的建议是，如果你上的一门课，老师讲得非常非常快，那么你可能更适合

sentences.en: off with the computer because if you can type faSt. If you're in a class in mathematics where they're
sentences.zh: 用电脑，因为如果你打字够快的话。如果你上的是数学课，老师在黑板上

sentences.en: putting lots of equations on the board, probably a computer is not going to work well.
sentences.zh: 写了很多方程式，那电脑可能就不太好用了。

sentences.en: You need to take longhand.
sentences.zh: 你需要手写。

sentences.en: So really, I think the jury is out about which is better.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，哪种方式更好尚无定论。

sentences.en: I would say neither is better, but really taking notes themselves, the magic happens after you get the good notes down, not while you're taking them.
sentences.zh: 我会说没有哪种更好，但真正做笔记，魔法发生在你记下好笔记之后，而不是在记笔记的过程中。

sentences.en: And Kim, I think it's really important to remember when we're talking about notes that there are three actual purposes to notes.
sentences.zh: 金，我认为在谈论笔记时，记住笔记的三个实际用途非常重要。

sentences.en: Yes, it's recording what happened, but it's an opportunity to review what's going on and then an opportunity to revise.
sentences.zh: 是的，它是记录所发生的事情，但它也是一个回顾所学内容的机会，然后是一个修改的机会。

sentences.en: And I think we've actually dedicated an entire chapter to note-taking just because it's so important and so underused.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为我们确实专门用了一整章来讨论做笔记，仅仅因为它太重要了，却又被严重低估。

sentences.en: So one other thing to keep in mind when everybody thinks about laptop versus longhand, I think what
sentences.zh: 所以当大家考虑笔记本电脑与手写笔记时，还有一点要记住，我认为

sentences.en: many of those studies, John's and others have found is there is an important additional factor
sentences.zh: 约翰和其他许多研究发现，当我们谈论笔记本电脑与手写笔记时，有一个重要的附加因素，

sentences.en: when we talk about laptop versus note hands is that any device that enables you to be distracted by something else can be problematic.
sentences.zh: 那就是任何让你容易分心的设备都可能是有问题的。

sentences.en: So you can be distracted if you're taking notes on a laptop and then you go to another tab and check your messages.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你用笔记本电脑做笔记，然后切换到另一个标签页查看消息，你就会分心。

sentences.en: Or you can be distracted if you're writing notes longhand and your phone notifies you and you decided to divide your attention and look at it.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你手写笔记，手机通知响了，你决定分心去看它，你也会分心。

sentences.en: That's really what's seeming to be that there's that collateral damage there of laptops make it more
sentences.zh: 这似乎就是笔记本电脑带来的附带损害，它们更容易

sentences.en: likely to switch tabs and be distracted, which I think contributes in a long, long way to them being problematic with note-taking.
sentences.zh: 让你切换标签页并分心，我认为这在很大程度上导致了它们在做笔记时出现问题。

sentences.en: So, you know, focus, cut down on those distractions.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，要专注，减少那些干扰。

sentences.en: You see, that's a theme we keep coming back to.
sentences.zh: 你看，这是我们不断提到的一个主题。

sentences.en: But boy, no matter what you're trying to learn, cutting down on these distractions is better.
sentences.zh: 但天哪，无论你想学什么，减少这些干扰总是更好的。

sentences.en: Now, what about cramming?
sentences.zh: 那么，临时抱佛脚呢？

sentences.en: I mean, every college student does it.
sentences.zh: 我是说，每个大学生都会这么做。

sentences.en: You know, you got a test tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 你知道，明天就要考试了。

sentences.en: Oh my God, you're panicking.
sentences.zh: 天哪，你很恐慌。

sentences.en: You're going to stay up all night and you're really just going to slam it.
sentences.zh: 你打算熬夜通宵，然后死记硬背。

sentences.en: Does it work?
sentences.zh: 这管用吗？

sentences.en: Does it get you maybe an A on the test?
sentences.zh: 它能让你在考试中拿到A吗？

sentences.en: But then what happens long term?
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看会发生什么呢？

sentences.en: I'm going to touch on just the knowledge component and I'll let Regan talk about how it disrupts sleep and performance and all that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我只谈知识层面，我会让里根谈谈它如何破坏睡眠和表现等等。

sentences.en: Certainly, depending on how difficult the test is, you can cram and get an A in your class.
sentences.zh: 当然，根据考试的难度，你可以临时抱佛脚并在课上拿到A。

sentences.en: And I want all students out there to know that often, that's fine.
sentences.zh: 我希望所有的学生都知道，通常情况下，这没问题。

sentences.en: You don't have to remember everything that you do in college.
sentences.zh: 你不必记住你在大学里学的所有东西。

sentences.en: That's okay.
sentences.zh: 那没关系。

sentences.en: But if you really want to know something well, really want to retain it, say it's part of a major,
sentences.zh: 但如果你真的想很好地掌握某样东西，真的想留存它，比如它是你专业的一部分，

sentences.en: or you're going to need this content, say for a subsequent advanced course, cramming likely will fail you.
sentences.zh: 或者你以后需要这些内容，比如为了后续的高级课程，临时抱佛脚很可能会让你失败。

sentences.en: Because what happens is you'll learn it kind of just well enough to recognize and perform, like pass that performance threshold for that exam.
sentences.zh: 因为你会学得刚好足够识别和表现，比如通过考试的门槛。

sentences.en: But then you'll quickly forget that knowledge that you learned.
sentences.zh: 但随后你会很快忘记所学的知识。

sentences.en: So, it won't be readily available when you take that advanced class, it'll be more difficult to relearn and so forth.
sentences.zh: 所以，当你上那门高级课程时，这些知识将无法随时调用，重新学习会更困难，等等。

sentences.en: So, that's why using these other strategies like space practice can benefit you in the long term because you'll retain that knowledge longer.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是为什么使用间隔练习等其他策略能让你长期受益，因为你会更持久地留存这些知识。

sentences.en: I still encourage my students because I know it makes them comfortable to study the night before.
sentences.zh: 我仍然鼓励我的学生在考前一晚复习，因为我知道这让他们感到安心。

sentences.en: But if they've used these other techniques, spacing, retrieval practice, and so forth,
sentences.zh: 但如果他们使用了其他技巧，比如间隔练习、提取练习等等，

sentences.en: getting ready, then that study session the night before will be an anxiety reducer because they'll realize they know the content well and that they're ready to go, right?
sentences.zh: 做好准备，那么考前那一晚的复习将是一种减轻焦虑的方式，因为他们会意识到自己很了解内容，准备好了，对吧？

sentences.en: But cramming the whole, pulling an all-nighter, I think that's a horrible idea.
sentences.zh: 但整个临时抱佛脚，熬通宵，我认为那是个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Regan probably always did it when he was in college, but I certainly never did.
sentences.zh: 里根上大学时可能总是这样，但我肯定从来没有。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: What do you think, Regan?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢，里根？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I like the rule that you tied in sleep in there because I think sleep is a pretty big deal.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢你把睡眠联系在一起的规则，因为我认为睡眠非常重要。

sentences.en: I think there are a lot of techniques that are not so much techniques, but life habits.
sentences.zh: 我认为有很多技巧与其说是技巧，不如说是生活习惯。

sentences.en: We spend the entire last chapter actually talking about eating and physical activity and sleep.
sentences.zh: 我们花了最后一整章的时间来讨论饮食、体育锻炼和睡眠。

sentences.en: But particularly in the context of cramming, I think the big part here to keep in mind is if that night before is your
sentences.zh: 但特别是在临时抱佛脚的情况下，我认为这里要记住的重要一点是，如果考前那一晚是你

sentences.en: first rural dedicated attention to the material, yeah, you need to find the next day, but that is going to erode and fade very, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 第一次真正投入精力去学习这些材料，是的，你第二天可能需要它，但这些知识会非常非常快地流失和消退。

sentences.en: And as long as you have the spacing in there, absolutely you're going to feel better studying a little bit some the night before.
sentences.zh: 只要你做好了间隔复习，考前一晚稍微复习一下绝对会让你感觉更好。

sentences.en: But I think
sentences.zh: 但我认为

sentences.en: how much sleep you get also makes a difference.
sentences.zh: 你的睡眠时长也起着关键作用。

sentences.en: One of the big reasons that there are many, many reasons to sleep a lot.
sentences.zh: 睡眠之所以重要，原因有很多很多。

sentences.en: I mean, there are a lot of functions of sleep that are important.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，睡眠有很多重要的功能。

sentences.en: But one of the ones most important to, I think, this conversation is sleep is a time when memory consolidation takes place.
sentences.zh: 但我认为与这次谈话最相关的一点是，睡眠是记忆巩固发生的时刻。

sentences.en: There's actual, and not just memory consolidation, but even studies show that even problem solving is enhanced by sleep.
sentences.zh: 事实上，不仅是记忆巩固，甚至有研究表明，睡眠还能增强解决问题的能力。

sentences.en: If you actually benefit by struggling on a problem, stopping and going to bed, then staying up until you've solved it.
sentences.zh: 如果你在解决难题时感到吃力，与其熬夜死磕，不如停下来去睡觉，这样反而更有益。

sentences.en: And when I actually benefit, there are some great experiments that literally have people work on a puzzle, then go to bed,
sentences.zh: 说到“更有益”，有一些很棒的实验：让人们研究一个谜题，然后去睡觉，

sentences.en: and lo and behold, those on waking up, they actually come up with a solution that they didn't have when they went to bed.
sentences.zh: 结果你猜怎么着，他们醒来后，竟然想出了睡前没能找到的解决方案。

sentences.en: So I think sleep before an exam is really important.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为考前睡眠真的很重要。

sentences.en: I also want to say it's not just before an exam.
sentences.zh: 我还想说，这不仅仅是考前那一晚的事。

sentences.en: More recent work on sleep shows that it's not just a day before an event that's important,
sentences.zh: 关于睡眠的最新研究表明，重要的不仅仅是考试前一天，

sentences.en: but the accumulated sleep that you get up to a week before an important exam or an important performance thing.
sentences.zh: 而是你在重要考试或重要表现前一周内累计的睡眠。

sentences.en: And this is stuff that just came out earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 这些研究成果是今年早些时候才发布的。

sentences.en: It's that accumulated sleep, because I've heard students say, oh, no, don't worry, Dr. Warren.
sentences.zh: 关键在于累计睡眠，因为我常听学生说：“哦，没关系，沃伦博士。”

sentences.en: I'll make sure I get enough sleep the night before.
sentences.zh: “我会确保考前那一晚睡够就行。”

sentences.en: And I say, it's not just the night before.
sentences.zh: 而我会告诉他们，不仅仅是考前那一晚。

sentences.en: It's, you know, a few days coming up.
sentences.zh: 而是，你知道，考前那几天都要保证睡眠。

sentences.en: But yeah, you know, that's the thing is, the bad news is students scram and they go, oh, I did well the next day.
sentences.zh: 但确实，坏消息是学生们会临时抱佛脚，然后说：“看，我第二天表现得挺好。”

sentences.en: And if that particular class doesn't have a cumulative final or a cumulative kind of test,
sentences.zh: 如果那门课没有期末总评或综合性考试，

sentences.en: they're not likely to realize that that cramming didn't serve them well.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能意识不到这种突击复习其实并没让他们真正掌握知识。

sentences.en: But particularly for those of our listeners who are no longer taking classes, this is even more important, right?
sentences.zh: 但对于我们那些已经不再上学的听众来说，这一点甚至更重要，对吧？

sentences.en: Because you want to spread it out, you want to space it, you want to practice retrieval, because we want to remember this for the rest of our lives, or at least for a long time.
sentences.zh: 因为你需要分散学习，需要间隔复习，需要练习提取记忆，因为我们希望终身记住这些知识，或者至少要记住很长一段时间。

sentences.en: And cramming will definitely not get you that.
sentences.zh: 而临时抱佛脚绝对做不到这一点。

sentences.en: So I want to ask where the teaching of critical thinking figures into your work.
sentences.zh: 我想问问，批判性思维的教学在你的工作中占什么地位？

sentences.en: Are there methods that can help people do better at this?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么方法能帮助人们在这方面做得更好？

sentences.en: I'm asking that question in light of all the missing disinformation that we're being bombarded with right now?
sentences.zh: 我提出这个问题是考虑到我们现在正被各种错误信息所轰炸。

sentences.en: Are some of the techniques that you talk about
sentences.zh: 你所谈到的一些技巧，

sentences.en: helpful in teaching students how to discern between things that are real and things that are fake?
sentences.zh: 是否有助于教学生如何辨别真假信息？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think the place that it comes in when I think about the book and be think about studying
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为当谈到这本书以及学习技巧时，

sentences.en: and study techniques in general is when we talk about deep processing, I mean, you know, when we set the
sentences.zh: 它涉及的核心就是我们所说的“深度加工”。我的意思是，当我们

sentences.en: stage in the first chapter, we talk about the importance of deeper processing.
sentences.zh: 在第一章铺垫时，我们就谈到了深度加工的重要性。

sentences.en: And very often, even when it comes to memory, questioning material leads to deeper processing.
sentences.zh: 通常情况下，即使在记忆方面，对材料进行质疑也会引导深度加工。

sentences.en: So for example, in cognitive science, we often talk about shallow processing versus deep processing.
sentences.zh: 例如，在认知科学中，我们经常谈论浅层加工与深层加工。

sentences.en: The example here is, if I ask you to memorize a list of words, and you just, you know, are, think about, does it have the letter E in it or the letter S in it?
sentences.zh: 举个例子，如果我让你背诵一串单词，而你只是在想：这个词里有没有字母E或字母S？

sentences.en: Well, that's a very quick decision.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是一个非常快速的判断。

sentences.en: Later on, when I ask you to remember the words, you're not really going to remember them.
sentences.zh: 稍后当我让你回忆这些单词时，你其实记不住它们。

sentences.en: On the other hand, if I ask you, when I read you a list of words, if I ask you, is this word a good word or a bad word?
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果我读给你一串单词，并问你：这个词是好词还是坏词？

sentences.en: Automatically, you're doing more work with it.
sentences.zh: 你自动就会对它进行更多的思考。

sentences.en: And lo and behold, you tend to remember more of the words that you've examined more deeply.
sentences.zh: 结果你猜怎么着，你往往能记住更多那些经过深度审视的单词。

sentences.en: Along those lines, when we actually critically think about words or information, that extra work that we do ongoing, wait, does this map onto my previous knowledge?
sentences.zh: 同样地，当我们真正批判性地思考词汇或信息时，我们所做的额外工作——比如“等等，这与我之前的知识相符吗？”——

sentences.en: And previous knowledge is very important with learning, right?
sentences.zh: 而先验知识对于学习非常重要，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, as an instructor, as a teacher, us knowing what that student already knows, as an adult learner, being aware of our
sentences.zh: 作为一名导师或教师，了解学生已有的知识，以及作为一名成年学习者，意识到我们的

sentences.en: experiences and our history becomes really important in how we face new information.
sentences.zh: 经验和背景，对于我们如何面对新信息变得非常重要。

sentences.en: And I think it's in those contexts, more indirectly, that we talk about critical thinking.
sentences.zh: 我认为正是在这些语境下，我们更间接地谈论了批判性思维。

sentences.en: Let me close by asking you this question.
sentences.zh: 最后我想问你一个问题。

sentences.en: Where do you think there are still knowledge gaps in understanding the best ways to teach?
sentences.zh: 你认为在理解最佳教学方法方面，还有哪些知识空白？

sentences.en: What are you looking at going forward for the second edition of your book?
sentences.zh: 在准备你的书的第二版时，你关注的重点是什么？

sentences.en: We have a lot of knowledge about what works best, right?
sentences.zh: 我们已经掌握了很多关于什么方法最有效的知识，对吧？

sentences.en: From personal hygiene, like brushing your teeth is a good idea.
sentences.zh: 就像个人卫生一样，刷牙是个好主意。

sentences.en: Flossing is a great idea.
sentences.zh: 用牙线也是个好主意。

sentences.en: Using retrieval practice and successive relearning, great idea.
sentences.zh: 使用提取练习和连续再学习，也是好主意。

sentences.en: However, say most of us know that flossing is wonderful and even understand the mechanisMs. How many of us really regularly floss?
sentences.zh: 然而，我们大多数人都知道用牙线很好，甚至理解其原理，但有多少人真的经常使用牙线呢？

sentences.en: And the question is, now that we have all this wonderful knowledge about how to live healthier lives, how to become a better student, how do we motivate students?
sentences.zh: 问题在于，既然我们拥有了所有关于如何过上更健康生活、如何成为更好学生的精彩知识，我们该如何激励学生呢？

sentences.en: How do we motivate ourselves to use these best practices?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何激励自己去使用这些最佳实践？

sentences.en: So as much as I believe myself that goal setting, planning and time management are tools for motivation, wow, I wish we had a chapter in
sentences.zh: 虽然我自己相信目标设定、规划和时间管理是激励的工具，但我真希望我们能有一章

sentences.en: there that described, look, these are tried and true techniques to help you motivate yourself to do the best things in the long run.
sentences.zh: 专门描述这些经过验证的技巧，来帮助你激励自己从长远来看去做最正确的事。

sentences.en: And I know there's some techniques students can use, but I know we need a lot moving in that direction to really develop really foolproof ways for motivation.
sentences.zh: 我知道学生可以使用一些技巧，但我知道我们需要在这一方向上做更多努力，才能真正开发出万无一失的激励方法。

sentences.en: So that would be my addition to the book.
sentences.zh: 所以那会是我对这本书的补充。

sentences.en: Dr. Gurung, what about you?
sentences.zh: 古隆博士，你呢？

sentences.en: Dr. Gurung, what about you?
sentences.zh: 古隆博士，你呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I actually think about, you know, and motivation is good.
sentences.zh: 是的，我确实在思考这个问题，激励固然重要。

sentences.en: I mean, we touch on motivation, we touch on, you know, getting social support and help when you need it, because that's really important.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们触及了激励，触及了在需要时寻求社会支持和帮助，因为这真的很重要。

sentences.en: That's definitely something that can be expanded on.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是可以扩展的内容。

sentences.en: But when I think about what's really needed here, I'm reminded of all the instructors, all the thousands and thousands
sentences.zh: 但当我思考这里真正需要什么时，我想到了所有的教师，成千上万

sentences.en: of instructors working so hard, who don't know, or were never trained in cognitive science or teaching, for that matter, and here I'm talking about higher education.
sentences.zh: 工作非常努力的教师，他们并不了解，或者从未接受过认知科学或教学方面的培训，我这里指的是高等教育领域。

sentences.en: You know, most of us in higher education with PhDs didn't necessarily have a teaching program.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们大多数拥有博士学位的高等教育工作者，并不一定接受过教学培训项目。

sentences.en: I mean, there were some great grad programs that did, but many teaching programs didn't.
sentences.zh: 当然，有一些很棒的研究生项目提供了培训，但许多教学项目并没有。

sentences.en: That's why, you know, APO's division on the Society for the Teaching of Psychology is great, such a great resource.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么美国心理学会（APA）的心理学教学分会是一个非常棒的资源。

sentences.en: But when I think about next edition of the book, I actually think of a compliment to the book.
sentences.zh: 但当我想起书的下一版时，我实际上想到的是这本书的配套读物。

sentences.en: And John, I think, here you go.
sentences.zh: 约翰，我想，就是这个。

sentences.en: First I knew heard of this, but it's, you know, next to study like a champion, I think we need teach like a champion.
sentences.zh: 虽然我是第一次听说这个想法，但我觉得，除了《像冠军一样学习》，我们还需要一本《像冠军一样教学》。

sentences.en: And, you know, where we really, we really address this book to students.
sentences.zh: 我们要真正地把这本书写给学生看。

sentences.en: So it's like, you know, we've taken out as much of the jargon as possible.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们已经尽可能去掉了所有的专业术语。

sentences.en: We've put in really pragmatic tips, but it's aimed at the student.
sentences.zh: 我们加入了非常实用的建议，但它是针对学生的。

sentences.en: And oh boy, yeah, I hope some, I hope many faculty sneak a copy in and, and, and, you know, get their training done pretty quickly.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我希望一些，我希望很多教职员工能偷偷看上一本，然后，你知道，快速完成他们的教学培训。

sentences.en: But I really see writing one completely directed at faculty, where we can help them anticipate the problems that students have.
sentences.zh: 但我确实想写一本完全针对教职员工的书，我们可以帮助他们预判学生遇到的问题。

sentences.en: And help them solve it.
sentences.zh: 并帮助他们解决这些问题。

sentences.en: Well, this has been really interesting.
sentences.zh: 好的，这次谈话真的很有意思。

sentences.en: I very much appreciate you're both joining me today.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你们两位今天能来参加我的节目。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thanks for having us.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我们。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Thanks so much, Kim.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢，Kim。
